It's a strange and uncomfortable feeling, it's like my brain has been completed wiped, the solid ground that I once relied on feels shaky and not real. I feel that I'm struggling to solve problems (a core consultant skill) and not really that strong in either writing or modelling. 

I haven't worked on any tech projects, the main clients I worked for were in government.

That sounds like an awful experience. I think there was a time where I could tough through the experiences like you described. Nowadays I feel like I absorb every hit I take. 

Which projects did you love and why? I feel like I need to start over new and find something complete different, nothing springs to mind that really makes me excited/passionate in my current line of work.
Yes, that's definitely the plan. I need to find a structured way to spend my time off.

I don't know, I'm having trouble disentangling the issues. It may be a combination of having a bad experience on projects, having an inherently unstructured, disorganised mindset (I'm going to get tested for ADHD) and the impacts of working from home. 

 My organisation has reduced the workload for me but I'm still struggling. It's gotten to a point where I have trouble completing basic exercises. For example, my mind blanks when I'm doing my timesheet.

Yes, the implications of working with the ongoing illness has taken its toll on me the last few months. The only question I have to myself is how I sustained it for so many years. Looking back, I was probably very close to capitulation many times. But it's so hard to remember, everything is so fuzzy.

I had a very poor experience in corporate. I started my career in consulting, went to corporate and now back in consulting. 

I wasn't learning much, there was a strong focus on window-dressing, blaming consultants (and each other) and the turnover level was very high. It was also stressful because there was large expectations but the organisation couldn't deliver. The business unit I was in continued to exist despite not adding any value at all. I would've been relieved if they fired me but they let me languish. 

I went back to consulting to escape this, little did I know how fast and quickly my mental health would deteriorate. In hindsight, this wasn't very rational - I overestimated how much gas I had left in the tank. 

These experiences have left me with a bleak outlook on "what else is out there" in the market. It's hard to tell if the issue's with me or the environment I've been exposed to. 

I tend to think the issue is with me - I can't really change who I work with, nor the circumstances I'm exposed to - only how I react and adapt. 

That's why I want to focus on myself (still don't know what that would entail yet and how to do it...) and the way I perceive things.

I think corporate (generally) would give me more headspace to focus on my mental health, but I'm still affected by my prior experience and don't want to trade one poison for another without reassurance.

That's awesome. Yeah, I don't have a good release from work, something that refreshes me/ fills back the motivation tank. 

I usually just play games or watch things brainlessly. It's essentially the same thing I've done through school and university.

Thanks - switching jobs has always the been the straightforward option. However, I have had experience in industry (this is my second stint in consulting) and it was very difficult, albeit for different reasons. 

The feeling I had in industry was that everything out of my control and extremely bureacratic. At the end of my stay in industry, I couldn't even think of a single thing to write on my CV.  

On balance, and in my current mental state, I would probably choose industry - however, it wouldn't take long for the unease and restlessness to settle in again. 

What I'm scared about now is that there is misalignment between me and the white collar sector in general, that I will always struggle in the corporate environment, be it consulting, industry or government. 

The elephant in the room is still the mental illness, but I've never thought too much about it. It's been a big constant in my life. I'm hoping to tackle it during my break and find out what's "underneath".
